newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila poultry firms seen reviving.
newsitem.headline: Manila poultry firms seen reviving.

text.p: Philippine poultry firms, bleeding from losses last year and in the first quarter of this year, are expected to make profits starting in second quarter 1997 due to firmer chicken prices, an industry official said on Thursday.
Bernardo Concepcion, president of the Philippine Association of Broiler Integrators, said local retail prices had increased to between 68 and 70 pesos per kg from last year's 60 pesos.
Chicken production this year is forecast to slow down to between 260 and 265 million kilos from last year's 290 to 300 million kilos.
Swift Foods Inc president Felicisimo Nacino had said earlier six of the country's largest poultry firms had agreed to cut output by an average 30 percent each to survive a glut.
"At 265 million kilos this year, supply is just enough to meet demand," Concepcion told reporters.
He said the local industry's losses reached 200 million pesos in the first three months of the year due to a glut.
The industry last year accumulated at least two billion pesos worth of losses.
